_what: Every identifier in this repository's PROSE, checked against PubMed for the publication types `Retracted Publication` and `Expression of Concern`. Swept 2026-09-01.
_why_it_exists: ⛔ BEFORE THIS, RETRACTION CHECKING RODE ON THE TYPE-CLAIM SCANNER AND THEREFORE COVERED ~1% OF THE CITATIONS. `lint_citation_types.evaluate()` raises a retraction advisory only for an identifier that a TYPE CLAIM reached — a sentence putting the identifier in the attributive slot after 'review', 'case report', 'meta-analysis' and so on. On 2026-09-01 that was 23 type claims against 13 cached records, out of 1,077 prose identifiers. A citation to a retracted paper that nobody happened to call 'a review' was invisible, and the guard's own green line said '23 type claim(s) checked' rather than 'the other 1,054 identifiers were not looked at'.
_attribution: According to PubMed. Publication types, titles, journals and DOIs here are PubMed's; PubMed's terms require attribution and a resolvable DOI link wherever its metadata travels, so every row that quotes a record carries `doi_url`.
_source_of_truth: PubMed, read through the PubMed MCP connector (`search_articles` with `"Retracted Publication"[Publication Type] OR "Expression of Concern"[Publication Type]`, `convert_article_ids`, `get_article_metadata`). Direct NCBI E-utilities are refused by this sandbox's egress proxy (CONNECT 403), which is why the connector is the fetcher and this file is what the gate READS.
_how_to_refresh: 1. Run `python3 research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py` and read the NOT SWEPT list — those are identifiers with no row here. 2. For each, resolve to a PMID (PubMed MCP `convert_article_ids`, id_type='pmcid' or 'doi'; note the ID Converter only covers PMC-backed records, so a DOI it cannot resolve still needs a `"<doi>"[doi]` search). 3. Batch the PMIDs into `(a[uid] OR b[uid] ...) AND ("Retracted Publication"[Publication Type] OR "Expression of Concern"[Publication Type])` — the connector refuses more than 20 boolean operators, so 17 identifiers per query is the ceiling. 4. Add a row per identifier. ⛔ Never add a row from recollection, and never mark an identifier `clean` because a lookup failed — that is what `unknown` is for.
_what_this_does_not_prove: A `clean` row means PubMed did not type that record `Retracted Publication` or `Expression of Concern` ON THE SWEEP DATE. It is not a statement that the paper is sound, that its claims replicate, or that it will not be retracted tomorrow — retraction is a moving target and this file is a dated observation. It also says nothing about the ~third of prose identifiers PubMed cannot see at all (arXiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, GEO, Zenodo, PDB, preprint and meeting-abstract DOIs); those are in `unknown` and they are UNKNOWN, not clean.

coverage._derived: regenerate with the generator described in _how_to_refresh; never edit by hand
